item.title: Joe Burrow: We found a way to win, we didn't do that the last few years
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they're ready to start playing football this season.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals apparently need to dig themselves a 13-0 hole before they're ready to start playing football this season.

The Bengals spotted the Ravens that lead in the first half of Week 7 before rallying for a 35-13 win and they found themselves down 13-0 in the first quarter against the Titans this Sunday. They didn't wait until the second half to get their act together this week, but they had to struggle the whole way before finally nailing down a 43-36 overtime win.

Burrow and others fielded questions about their slow starts in their postgame press conferences, but Burrow was more interested in the final scores because he feels that scrapping out wins like their last two are a sign that the team has fixed part of what has ailed them the last few years.

"We found a way to win today. We're 5-2," Burrow said, via a transcript from the team. "We lose that game for the last three years. It's hard to win. You want to be great snap in snap out, but it's not the reality of it. All we can do is keep working hard and get better. You win from wins and losses and good plays and bad plays. That's what the NFL and getting better is. We'll continue to do that."

Burrow threw three interceptions to go with five touchdown passes and his game-winning touchdown run on Sunday. He acknowledged the need to "be better and limit those critical mistakes," but returned often to the theme of finding ways to win when they would have fallen apart in the past.

item.title: Joe Brady: Sunday's performance is the expectation for our defense
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bills allowed an average of 28.5 points per game in their first six games of the 2026 season and improving on that was a focus for the team during their bye week.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills allowed an average of 28.5 points per game in their first six games of the 2026 season and improving on that was a focus for the team during their bye week.

Sunday's return to action resulted in much better numbers. They allowed the Ravens 144 yards in a 36-10 win that moved their record to 6-1 on the season. After the game was over, head coach Joe Brady said he wants the unit to look at that performance as their standard for the rest of the season.

"I think our defense should look at today and understand that that’s what the expectation is," Brady said, via the team's website. "And I'm not talking about the production. I'm not talking about the takeaways and sacks. I'm talking about the style that they played, the way that they flew around. Look, I'm just watching it out there, but I think the silent tape's going to speak loudly in terms of the way that they played for one another, the way they ran around, the communication. Everything we challenged them with coming off the bye, I thought they responded to it, and they just kept going."

Brady's message was about the defense, but it's hard to ignore what was going on for the Ravens offense. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both left the game with injuries, which meant undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was pressed into action for the first time in the NFL.

Fagnano was overmatched, but future Bills opponents won't be quite so hamstrung and the Buffalo defense will have to show that they are able to match that level of play against all comers.

item.title: Khalil Mack trying to be where his "feet are at" amid trade rumors
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chargers slumped to another defeat on Sunday and most of the attention being paid to the 0-7 team concerns who is going to be hitting the road in the near future.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers slumped to another defeat on Sunday and most of the attention being paid to the 0-7 team concerns who is going to be hitting the road in the near future.

Some of those conversations have to do with firing coaches and some have to do with potential trades of veteran players. Linebacker Khalil Mack is one of those players as he is playing on a one-year deal and has the kind of history of success as a pass rusher that could be appealing to a number of teams.

After Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams, Mack was asked about his mindset amid the trade chatter.

“You’ve got to be where your feet are man, ultimately," Mack said, via Eric Williams of Fox Sports. "That can be the most difficult thing when you’re dealing with a lot of outside noise and stuff. Just trying to be where your feet are at all time. That’s kind of been my thing in years past.”

The trade deadline is a week from Tuesday, so Mack, who has three sacks this season, will know where his feet will be for the rest of the season in the near future.

item.title: Saquon Barkley: Eagles said they won't trade me, I want to be here to fix it
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A report before Sunday's games said that the Eagles will not trade running back Saquon Barkley ahead of the November 10 trade deadline and Barkley said after Sunday night's game against the Commanders that he's received the same message from the team.
item.content:encoded:
A report before Sunday's games said that the Eagles will not trade running back Saquon Barkley ahead of the November 10 trade deadline and Barkley said after Sunday night's game against the Commanders that he's received the same message from the team.

Barkley played through hamstring and back injuries in that game and he scored a touchdown in the first quarter, but the Eagles went from being up 10-0 to losing 27-10 in Washington. The loss was the sixth in a row for a team that's reeling, but Barkley made it clear that he's not looking to jump ship and is happy that the Eagles aren't interested in parting ways.

"When that message was relayed to me, it definitely does mean a lot," Barkley said, via Tim McManus of ESPN.com. "The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I'm the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it, and I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it."

The Eagles traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens last month and their tailspin would seem to make more deals a real possibility, but Barkley is set to be around for the long haul.

item.title: Dan Campbell wisely declined the Vikings' intentional offsides
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: With 2:00 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday in Detroit, the Lions had a 19-15 lead and the ball, facing second-and-2.
item.content:encoded:
With 2:00 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday in Detroit, the Lions had a 19-15 lead and the ball, facing second-and-2. Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel jumped offside, and fans in Detroit cheered, thinking the Vikings had made a mistake. But Lions coach Dan Campbell knew better.

Campbell declined the penalty because he knew the Vikings had jumped offside on purpose, wanting to concede a first down while the clock was stopped so that they could then use their three timeouts after the Lions' first, second and third-down plays and then get the ball back with time left for a comeback drive.

Tom Brady, calling the game on Fox, immediately recognized what was happening.

"They're not gonna accept that," Brady said as soon as Van Ginkel jumped. "They'll decline that penalty."

It was obvious to Brady, but it wasn't obvious to Bears coach Ben Johnson when he faced the same situation against the Patriots. Coach Mike Vrabel told his team to jump offside to concede a first down, and Johnson accepted the penalty. That allowed the Patriots to use their three timeouts on the Bears' next three plays, forcing the Bears to kick on fourth down with 1:38 remaining. The Bears ended up winning when kicker Cairo Santos made it a two-possession game with a 58-yard field goal, but if the Bears had missed, Johnson's decision to accept the penalty could have proven costly.

It's a situation that doesn't arise in most games, but it happens often enough that every coach should understand it as well as Vrabel, Campbell and Brady do: Sometimes, the smart thing for one team is to commit a penalty on purpose, and the smart thing for the other team is to decline the penalty.

In theory, if the defensive team continued to jump offside and the offense continued to decline the penalties, it could reach the point where the referee would have to warn the defensive team's head coach that he could invoke the "palpably unfair act" rule, which gives the referee wide leeway to use his own discretion to enforce penalties. The referee could, for instance, charge the defensive team a timeout if it refused to stop committing intentional penalties.

It didn't reach that point on Sunday, as Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell realized that Campbell was on to the intentional offside. Campbell is a smart in-game coach who recognized on Sunday what the right strategic decision was in the final two minutes.

item.title: Larry Csonka celebrates Vikings' loss as 1972 Dolphins stand alone for another year
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: It's celebration time for the 1972 Dolphins.
item.content:encoded:
It's celebration time for the 1972 Dolphins.

After the Vikings' loss to the Lions on Sunday, there are no remaining undefeated teams in the NFL. That means the 1972 Dolphins will remain, for at least another year, the only perfect, undefeated, untied team in NFL history.

Larry Csonka, the 79-year-old fullback who was the 1972 Dolphins' leading rusher, posted a picture of himself having a celebratory cigar and a drink on social media.

"CONGRATS to the #DetroitLions on the Win and a game well played today," Csonka wrote. "CHEERS to all my ‘72 undefeated teammates and #MiamiDolphin fans on our now 54 year record! Cheers!"

The 1972 Dolphins finished the regular season 14-0 and then won two playoff games and Super Bowl VII to finish a perfect 17-0. Players on that team have continued to celebrate their status as the only perfect team in the NFL's 107-year history.

item.title: Nick Sirianni: I am not doing a good enough job, I've got to do better
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Eagles' head coach took the blame after Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles coach Nick Sirianni took the blame after Sunday night's loss to the Commanders.

The Eagles, who started the season 2-0 and had Super Bowl aspirations, lost their sixth consecutive game to fall to 2-6. Sirianni said the head coach deserves the blame when that happens.

“I take everything as my responsibility that happens out on that field. Everything. Obviously I am not doing a good enough job right now. I've got to do better," Sirianni said.

Asked if offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will remain the play caller, Sirianni didn't answer directly.

"I'm not thinking about any of that stuff right now," Sirianni said.

But Sirianni did say the ultimate responsibility for turning the Eagles around is his, not any assistant coach's.

"That falls on me," Sirianni said. "With all the detail that’s not happening right now, I’ve got to try a different approach. That 100 percent is on me with how many of those issues are happening right now. I’ll do everything I can to do different things to get that point across."

Sirianni said the Eagles are determined to turn their season around.

"I'm pissed at myself," Sirianni said. "I know I'll fight like hell to do everything I can do to get this fixed."

item.title: Sunday Night Football: Commanders roll to 27-10 victory over Eagles
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Philadelphia took a 10-0 lead early, but didn't score again. The Eagles have now lost six consecutive games.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders have gotten back in the win column.

While Philadelphia took a 10-0 lead in the first quarter, it was all Washington from then on, with the club coming away with a 27-10 victory on Sunday night.

With Tanner McKee starting his third game in place of Jalen Hurts, Washington’s defense thoroughly outplayed Philadelphia’s offense throughout the night. The Commanders were able to generate pressure on McKee, sacking him four times. Washington ended the night with nine official QB hits.

Saquon Barkley was limited to just 30 yards on 13 carries, including a 3-yard touchdown midway through the first quarter.

Jake Elliott had a shot at another field goal in the fourth quarter, but a 41-yard attempt banged off the left upright. He had made a 36-yard attempt that was negated by a penalty for an illegal formation.

In many ways, that sequence encapsulated what’s been a rough 2026 for the Eagles.

Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels finished the night 16-of-29 for 217 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions.

It’s the first time Daniels has won a game since Oct. 2025.

Treylon Burks led with three catches for 81 yards. Stefon Diggs has three catches for 38 yards with a game-tying touchdown in the second quarter.

Drew Stevens gave Washington a three-point lead at halftime with a 39-yard field goal. Stevens also hit from 56 in the first quarter, 25 in the third quarter, and 42 in the fourth.

For the Eagles, this is the franchise’s first six-game losing streak since 2012. The last time the team started 2-6 was 1999. Both of those instances came under former head coach Andy Reid, in his last and first seasons with the club, respectively.

Philadelphia will host the 4-2-1 Giants next weekend.

With the win, the Commanders are now 2-4-1 and will host the 4-4 Rams in Week 9.

item.title: Chiefs, Steelers, Commanders have interest in Brian Thomas Jr.
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Contenders usually aren't sellers at the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Contenders usually aren't sellers at the trade deadline. But the Jaguars have a receiver who, for whatever reason, hasn't really clicked with the coaching staff that arrived in 2025.

As a result, 2024 first-rounder Brian Thomas Jr. has interest in a fresh start. And multiple teams are believed to be interested in acquiring him.

Currently, the Chiefs, Steelers, and Commanders have interest.

The Steelers, we're told, have greater interest in Colts receiver Josh Downs. Downs, however, is Kansas City's Plan B, if they can't get Thomas away from the Jaguars.

Thomas had 1,282 receiving yards as a rookie. In 2025, his output dipped to 707 yards. This year, Thomas has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns.

During Sunday's 42-7 romp over the Colts, Thomas was targeted twice, catching one pass for 12 yards and the first touchdown of the day.

The Jaguars have no real incentive to move him, unless they get a big offer. The problem is that their price tag doesn't reflect his current usage.

Beyond the question of whether they'd trade him at all is whether they'd send him to an AFC contender.

The Commanders aren't much of a contender at all this season; they'd presumably want Thomas for 2027 and, once the fifth-year option is exercised, 2028.

Still, trading him carries risk. If, once he's gone, Jakobi Meyers or Parker Washington get injured, the Jaguars will wish they still had him.

item.title: Kyler Murray developed hamstring tightness late in Sunday's loss
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray developed hamstring tightness sometime late in the fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray developed hamstring tightness sometime late in the fourth quarter. He said it was late enough that it didn't affect him in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.

But Murray will undergo further evaluation on Monday.

"We’ll look at it, obviously, and do what we need to do," Murray said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.

Murray went into the sideline medical tent after throwing a touchdown pass with 8:44 remaining. He was back on the field for the next drive.

It is unclear whether that was related to the hamstring issue or something else.

"Kyler Murray just [had] some hamstring tightness, and he was able to return late in the football game," coach Kevin O'Connell said.

Murray completed 17 of 29 passes for 210 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He ran for 35 yards on four carries.

item.title: Frustrated Justin Jefferson didn't speak to reporters after Sunday's loss
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: When a team is winning, it's hard for any offensive players who aren't getting the ball as often as they should to be upset.
item.content:encoded:
When a team is winning, it's hard for any offensive players who aren't getting the ball as often as they should to be upset. When winning becomes losing, the frustrations can quickly surface.

That happened for the Vikings on Sunday against the Lions. Receiver Justin Jefferson, who made a spectacular touchdown catch in the first half, didn't see the ball as often as he should have during proverbial nut-cutting time.

After the Vikings' final drive — which curiously ended on a fourth-and-five punt with 3:01 to play at a time when the Detroit rushing game was clicking — Jefferson made a rare display of frustration. After the 19-15 loss, Jefferson declined to speak to reporters, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.

Which means that Jefferson, who has a habit of always saying all the right things, doubted that he would have been able to do that.

"Obviously he's frustrated, and that's understandable," quarterback Kyler Murray told reporters, via Seifert. "He is who he is, and he has every right to the way he feels when he doesn't get the ball. That's on us to find a way to get him the ball."

"We had some opportunities for [Jefferson], and there were some chances there," coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters. "But we've got to find a way to get him the ball, especially on potential chances for him on some of those sequences where we're looking to kick off some momentum. He's a great guy to do it behind, and we'll continue to find ways to get him the football. But it was a division game. These guys want to win. I don't fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form."

Whatever the cause, there's clearly a problem. And Murray, who missed time early in the season due to a concussion, should be up to speed now. On Sunday, he wasn't good enough.

And here's the basic reality. At some point, either en route to the playoffs or after the Vikings get there, Murray will have to make a big play in a big spot. The jury is out on whether he will.

The Vikings don't have many options. They could try to make a trade, but who's out there? They wanted to keep Daniel Jones after the 2024 season; maybe, at this point, the Colts would welcome the chance to move on.

If the Raiders had lost to the Jets, Kirk Cousins may have been available for a reunion. With Las Vegas now at 4-4, why would they move him?

The other option would be to ride with Carson Wentz, who has shown that he can and will get the ball to Jefferson.

However it goes, Sunday's game exposed the biggest problem with the Vikings. Against teams that can't be held to 15 points or less, the Vikings may not be able to muster enough points to beat them.

item.title: Sunday Night Football: After going down 10-0, Commanders lead Eagles 13-10 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Philadelphia took an early 10-0 lead before Washington scored 13 straight points.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders got down 10-0, but have scored 13 straight points and have a 13-10 lead at halftime.

However, there could be an injury concern with Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels.

Daniels took a hard hit from Nolan Smith late in the first half on an incomplete pass and took a bit to get up. Though Marcus Mariota spoke with Daniels on the sideline, the young quarterback stayed in before throwing an incomplete pass on third-and-1 to bring up Drew Stevens’ 39-yard field goal with 19 seconds left on the clock.

The NBC broadcast showed Daniels wincing on the sideline as he went to sit down following the incomplete pass. Washington’s medical staff surrounded Daniels, but then the broadcast showed Daniels sitting by himself, ostensibly OK.

Daniels had a middling first half, completing 11-of-221 passes for 96 yards with a touchdown — an 8-yard pass to Stefon Diggs midway through the second quarter.

On the other side, Tanner McKee is 8-of-14 for 81 yards. Saquon Barkley had a 3-yard touchdown midway through the first quarter to make the score 10-0. He is having a tough night, though, gaining just 15 yards on eight carries. He also has a 24-yard reception.

The Eagles have just seven first downs, 113 total yards, and are 1-of-6 on third down.

Washington has 10 first downs, 185 yards, and is 4-of-9 on third down.

The Eagles will receive the second-half kickoff.

The Broncos entered Sunday with four players listed as questionable. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring) and left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) are all active.

All four players were limited in practice on both Thursday and Friday.

Cornerback Pat Surtain II is also officially active and will play for the first time since Week 4 when he injured his ankle.

The Broncos' inactives are quarterback Sam Ehlinger, safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), offensive lineman Gavin Ortega, offensive lineman Kage Casey, tight end Dallen Bentley, defensive lineman Jordan Jackson and defensive tackle Tyler Onyedim.

The Chiefs' inactives are cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), quarterback Garrett Nussmeier, offensive tackle Diego Pounds, defensive end Jack Pyburn, fullback Ben VanSumeren and defensive end Tyreke Smith. Nussmeier is the emergency, third quarterback.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson entered Sunday's game with 28 touches for 171 yards.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs rookie running back Emmett Johnson entered Sunday's game with 28 touches for 171 yards. He has three catches for 119 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos.

He scored a 73-yard touchdown, the longest touchdown play and longest reception for the Chiefs since Tyreek Hill went 75 yards against the Browns on Sep. 12, 2021. He also had a 38-yard reception to set up a 45-yard Harrison Butker field goal with 19 seconds left in the first half.

The Chiefs lead the Broncos 17-13 at halftime.

Kansas City outgained Denver 224 to 154 in the first half as Patrick Mahomes went 13-for-19 for 196 yards and two touchdowns. Rashee Rice scored on an 11-yard catch, and he has four catches for 38 yards.

Kenneth Walker has only 26 yards on seven carries.

Bo Nix is 11-of-19 for 121 yards and a touchdown, a 1-yard toss to Jaylen Waddle on fourth down. Courtland Sutton had two catches for 41 yards.

Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis has a sack and two batted passes.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes' third TD gives Chiefs a 24-13 lead
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Chiefs have opened it up against the Broncos, taking a 24-13 lead late in the third quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs have opened it up against the Broncos, taking a 24-13 lead late in the third quarter.

Tight end Noah Gray caught a 4-yard touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes with 1:38 left in the third quarter. It completed an 11-play, 63-yard drive.

Mahomes completed an 11-yard pass to Gray on third-and-6 and then completed a 12-yard pass to Cyrus Allen on third-and-12.

The Chiefs have 16 plays for 78 yards in the second half. The Broncos have nine plays for 19 yards since halftime, with three three-and-outs.

Mahomes is 22-of-31 for 254 yards and three touchdowns today.

The Chiefs have ruled out defensive lineman Peter Woods with a neck injury.

item.title: Broncos' goal-line stand holds off Chiefs 28-24 for division lead
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Broncos, who have four comeback wins this season, are 6-2.
item.content:encoded:
In a game they probably shouldn't have won, the Broncos beat the Chiefs with a goal-line stand in the final seconds.

Denver stopped Kansas City four times inside the 10-yard line, winning 28-24 for Sean Payton's 200th career victory, including the postseason. The Broncos lead the AFC West at 6-2, while the Chiefs fell to 5-2 with a second consecutive loss.

Denver trailed 24-13 in the fourth quarter before scoring 15 consecutive points for its fourth comeback win of the season.

The Chiefs uncharacteristically fell apart when it mattered most.

They had a chance to pad their lead, but Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal wide right with 2:31 remaining. It came after Alex Singleton sacked Patrick Mahomes for 6-yard loss.

Butker is in danger of losing his job after the Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad last week. The 10-year veteran has missed 6 of 17 field-goal attempts this season, including two misses in last week's loss to the Seahawks.

Two plays, 56 yards and 35 seconds later, the Broncos led for the first time. Jonah Coleman had a 51-yard catch-and-run before a 5-yard touchdown run. The Broncos led 28-24 with 1:56 left.

Emmett Johnson, the star for the Chiefs on Sunday, returned the kickoff 44 yards to the Kansas City 44, and two plays later, Mahomes found Travis Kelce for a 32-yard gain to the Denver 18.

The Chiefs had first-and-goal at the 4 with 35 seconds left. Kenneth Walker ran for 3 yards to the 1 before Patrick Surtain tackled him; Mahomes threw incomplete; and Walker was stopped for no gain by safety JL Skinner. That set up a final play with four seconds left, and after a false start, Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes to end the game.

The Chiefs outgained the Broncos 399 to 294 as Mahomes went 30-of-41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns. Johnson caught five passes for 128 yards and a touchdown and had a 15-yard run. Kelce added five catches for 67 yards.

Bo Nix was 20-of-32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, going 5-of-6 for 84 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Coleman had 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown and four catches for 63 yards.

item.title: Andy Reid: I didn't see a false start on Jaylon Moore at end of game
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chiefs blew an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Broncos, but they were able to drive back into position to try for a game-winning touchdown in the final seconds.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs blew an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Broncos, but they were able to drive back into position to try for a game-winning touchdown in the final seconds.

That effort looked like it was successful when Patrick Mahomes flipped a pass to wide receiver Rashee Rice in the end zone with four seconds to play, but the play had been whistled dead due to a false start on right tackle Jaylon Moore. Mahomes was sacked on the next snap and the Broncos celebrated a 28-24 win.

Moore's movement was minimal enough that Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said at his postgame press conference that he thought the call was incorrect.

“I didn’t see it," Reid said. "That’s one man’s opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see a false start.”

Moore also appeared to twitch his leg prior to the snap, which may not change Reid's opinion but it was enough for a costly penalty that helped send the Chiefs to a second straight loss.

item.title: Sean Payton is the sixth-fastest coach to 200 wins
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Broncos coach (and long-time Saints coach) Sean Payton was going for his 200th career win on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos coach (and long-time Saints coach) Sean Payton was going for his 200th career win on Sunday. And he got it.

It's one thing to get to 200. It's another thing to get there quickly, relative to others.

Payton is the sixth-fastest to 200 wins. He got there in 320 games.

The other five are Hall of Famers, with the exception of one who should be a Hall of Famer. Don Shula got there in 286 games. George Halas made it in 287 games. Curly Lambeau made it in 300 games. Bill Belichick made it in 307 games. And Paul Brown made it in 309 games.

Behind Payton is another Hall of Famer — Tom Landry. He got there in 325 games.

The other coaches with 200 or more wins are Andy Reid, Chuck Noll, Marty Schottenheimer, Mike Tomlin, and Dan Reeves.

Payton will now chase Reeves and Tomlin, who have 201 wins each, Schottenheimer, who has 205, and Noll, who has 209.

After that, it's Brown with 222, Lambeau with 229, and Landry with 270.

item.title: Justin Herbert has gone eight straight starts without multiple TDs
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the 0-6 Chargers emerge from their bye with a "visit" to the Rams, quarterback Justin Herbert will be trying to reverse a horrible trend.
item.content:encoded:
As the 0-6 Chargers emerge from their bye with a "visit" to the Rams, quarterback Justin Herbert will be trying to reverse a horrible trend.

Herbert has gone eight straight games, including the postseason, without multiple total touchdowns. Via NBC Sports research, only one quarterback in Chargers history has gone at least nine straight starts without multiple touchdowns.

The record is held by former first-rounder Ryan Leaf, who went 12 straight starts without multiple touchdowns from 1998 through 2000.

Herbert also leads the league with 10 turnovers. The Chargers nevertheless are sticking with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, at least for now.

An embarrassment against the team with which they share a stadium could change things, quickly.

item.title: Rams take 10-9 halftime lead with Kyren Williams 1-yard TD
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: While the Rams’ offense was largely listless for the first 30 minutes of Sunday’s game against the Chargers, the team woke up late in the second quarter.
item.content:encoded:
While the Rams’ offense was largely listless for the first 30 minutes of Sunday’s game against the Chargers, the team woke up late in the second quarter.

The Rams lead the contest between the two Los Angeles teams 10-9 at halftime.

The Rams did not have a first down until Matthew Stafford connected with Tutu Atwell for a 40-yard gain down the left side with 1:26 remaining in the half — putting the Rams at the Chargers’ 17-yard line. From there, Stafford hit Puka Nacua for a 13-yard gain to the 1-yard line.

Kyren Williams bounced his way into the end zone with a 1-yard run, with Brandon McManus connecting on the extra point to give the Rams a one-point advantage.

Stafford finished the first half 10-of-14 for 95 yards with an interception. Nacua leads with seven catches for 40 yards.

With so few plays, the Rams had just five rushing attempts in the half. Blake Corum had three for 8 yards while Williams had just two for 2 yards with the TD.

On the other side, Justin Herbert threw an interception on the Chargers’ third drive. But after that, he led the team to three consecutive field goals, with Cameron Dicker hitting from 34, 46, and 41 yards.

The Chargers nearly scored on their last drive of the half on a Hail Mary, but by the time Ladd McConkey could get possession of the football, he was outside the end zone and the second quarter was over.

Herbert was 14-of-20 for 181 yards with an interception in the first half. McConkey leads with four catches for 86 yards.

The Rams have just 90 yards of offense to the Chargers’ 219. But they will have a chance to double up, as the Rams will receive the second-half kickoff.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons

item.content:encoded:
The Chargers' offense remains poor with coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert.

Herbert threw his league-leading 10th interception in the third quarter of Sunday's game, and the Rams turned that into a touchdown to take a 24-9 lead with 3:41 left in the period.

Herbert was looking for tight end Charlie Kolar but found cornerback Trent McDuffie instead for the QB’s second interception of the game.

McDuffie returned it to the Chargers’ 22-yard line.

A play later, quarterback Matthew Stafford hit Puka Nacua with a screen pass on the left side, which the receiver took in for an 18-yard touchdown.

Nacua now leads with 10 catches for 82 yards on 11 targets.

Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is questionable to return after going down in the third quarter.

item.title: Rams dominate second half, defeat Chargers 24-9
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Rams scored 21 unanswered points to beat the Chargers, sending the cross-town team to 0-7 in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams’ offense looked ugly for much of the first half of Sunday’s cross-town matchup with the Chargers.

But the Rams took the lead with a successful two-minute drive and ended up scoring 21 unanswered points to win 24-9.

The Rams did not have a first down until Matthew Stafford connected with Tutu Atwell for a 40-yard gain down the left side with 1:26 remaining in the half. That led to Kyren Williams’ 1-yard touchdown with 19 seconds remaining in the second quarter.

Then the Rams doubled up with Blake Corum’s 23-yard touchdown run at the start of the second half, putting the team up 17-9.

Following Justin Herbert’s second interception of the day, Puka Nacua took a screen pass 18 yards for a touchdown to give the Rams a 15-point advantage.

Nacua ended the day with 11 receptions for 80 yards on 12 targets.

Matthew Stafford finished 17-of-25 for 157 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

While the Rams had just 10 yards rushing at the end of the first half, they ended up with 129 with a strong performance in the second half.

Corum led with 73 yards on 11 carries with a TD while Williams had 56 yards on 16 carries.

It was another ugly day for Herbert and the Chargers’ offense, which did not reach the end zone on the day. Herbert finished 24-of-32 for 257 yards with two picks. Quentin Lake had the first pick during the first quarter, leading to a Brandon McManus 30-yard field goal.

Trent McDuffie had the second pick.

Ladd McConkey led with four catches for 86 yards.

The Rams do have a pair of injury concerns at cornerback. First Jaylen Watson had to exit and did not return with a shoulder issue. Then McDuffie suffered a back injury and had to be sidelined.

The Rams have now won back-to-back games for the first time this season. At 4-4, the Rams will be on the road to face the Commanders in Week 9.

At 0-7, the reeling Chargers will be at home to face the Texans next weekend.

item.title: Sean McVay saw some good, some bad from having two kickers active vs. Chargers
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Rams took the unusual step today of having a field goal kicker, a kickoff kicker and a punter all active against the Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams took the unusual step today of having a field goal kicker, a kickoff kicker and a punter all active against the Chargers. Rams coach Sean McVay said after the game that proved to be a mixed bag.

Brandon McManus made all four of his kicks, three extra points and a 30-yard field goal. Joshua Karty, who was active just to kick kickoffs, was called for a kickoff short of the landing zone on two of his five kickoffs, which McVay was not happy about, although McVay said that when Karty actually got it into the landing zone, they were good kicks that were hard for the Chargers to return.

"The kickoff coverage doing a really nice job," McVay said. "We can't have the two penalties that put the ball on the 40-yard line, but I did think Josh hit some of those early ones really well. What led to us having two kickers up was really just that. That was a unit that we've felt like we've had successful outcomes with Josh kicking some of those squib or those dirty balls. He'll keep getting better at it. Sometimes your roster might not allow you to be able to do that, but that was the thinking."

McVay said having two kickers active is unusual but valuable if the kickoff kicker can prevent long returns.

"The thought process behind it was we had not been having any success covering kicks," McVay said. "We've got to be better in that area, but you did see when we were able to cover it, because he hits a really good ball that's hard to field. . . . They're not going to be able to field it clean and we're getting a start before they're getting their return set up, that was the thinking behind it. But obviously we did not want to have two plays that put it on the 40, where you're kicking it short of the landing zone."

Special teams have frequently been a problem for the Rams during McVay’s tenure as head coach, but he's eager to fix that problem, and that might mean having more players active on game days just to play special teams.

The Dolphins got their first win of the season in Week 7 and it seems they've developed a taste for victory.

Quarterback Malik Willis zipped a one-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Malik Washington with eight seconds to play in the first half and the Dolphins extended their lead to 13-3 before the halftime break in Miami.

The Dolphins' touchdown completed a big swing that started when Patriots kicker Andy Borregales missed a 40-yard field goal before the two minute warning. Willis completed five passes on the ensuing drive and Patriots linebacker Christian Elliss picked up a costly personal foul for lighting up Washington away from the play on one of them.

Wide receiver Efton Chism made another big mistake for the Patriots when he lost the ball after a short gain and the Dolphins recovered to set up one of Zane Gonzalez's field goals. Those errors along with a strong half from Willis have the Patriots in need of a big comeback to avoid a second straight loss.

They may not have tight end Hunter Henry to help with the effort. He is called questionable to return with a foot injury.

Maye's touchdown pass on the previous Patriots possession was initially and incomprehensibly ruled incomplete by referee Alex Moore's crew, which necessitated a successful challenge by Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. item.title: Patriots rally in second half for 24-19 win in Miami
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Drake Maye came alive after halftime and the Patriots improved to 5-3.
item.content:encoded:
The Patriots have had some rough trips to Miami in the past and it looked like this might be another one through the first 30 minutes of play, but things took a positive turn after halftime.

The Dolphins led 13-3 at the break, but the Patriots scored the first 21 points of the second half to build a two-score lead of their own. The Dolphins cut into that just before the two minute warning on a 35-yard Kevin Coleman touchdown catch, but they missed the extra point and the Patriots were able to run out the clock on a 24-19 win after recovering the onside kick.

Running back Rhamondre Stevenson picked up the final yards and he had 18 carries for 77 yards overall, but quarterback Drake Maye was in the center of the action for the Patriots' comeback.

After going 7-of-10 for 53 yards while being sacked twice in the first half, Maye completed eight straight passes to open the second half. Those passes picked up 144 yards and two of them went for touchdowns that covered more than 40 yards. The first was to Kyle Williams and the other was a short throw to Pop Douglas that Douglas turned into a 48-yard score in the fourth quarter.

Douglas's touchdown came a couple of plays after safety Kevin Byard's first interception as a Patriot. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis's throw went off of Patriots defensive lineman DaQuan Jones's helmet and spun into the air before coming down to Byard for Miami's first turnover of the game.

Maye also ran for a two-yard score and it makes two weeks in a row that Maye has produced points with his arm and his legs. It's also five straight games with multiple touchdown passes for Maye, which is made all the more impressive given how little of that success has come with wide receiver A.J. Brown playing a meaningful role on the New England offense.

Brown missed Sunday's game with a knee injury and the 5-3 Patriots will wait to see if he's able to return for next Sunday's game against the Packers.

Willis was 21-of-32 for 211 yards and two touchdowns, which makes it two straight strong performances for the first-year starter in Miami. Running back Ollie Gordon added 19 carries for 69 yards, but had a costly unsportsmanlike conduct penalty after one of his runs and the Dolphins don't have the kind of margin for error that allows them to overcome mistakes on a regular basis.

They'll stay at home for a visit from the Lions in Week 9 and the 1-5 club will need to be sharper if they want to pull off an upset in that matchup.
